subject: Priv Deploy: IAC GitOps bridge & composition review
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acme.co>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Infra Team <acme-infra@consultants.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Priv deploy - GitOps bridge proposal + diagram

Hi Nikhil / team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, we put together a short proposal for the GitOps bridge pattern we want to adopt to connect our on-prem VPC stacks with Redwood's private control plane. The two core asks:

- Keep our Terraform module boundaries (network / security / compute) intact so we can maintain internal change control.
- Allow Redwood's GitOps operator to apply only helm charts and light-weight overlay kustomize changes (no direct tfstate writes).

Attached is the deployment diagram (acme-priv-deploy-diagram-v2.png) and a one-page proposal (gitops-bridge-proposal.md) that sketches the bridge connector (ssh/bastion jump + signed artifact registry).

Open questions for you:
1) What CI gate(s) do you need before Redwood's operator can apply overlays?
2) How do you want to handle secrets: KMS wrap vs. per-cluster vault?
3) Can we get a short preflight test matrix to include in our PR check?

Looking to align this week so we can start a small pilot.

Thanks,
Maria Lopez\Director, Platform Engineering\Acme Analytics

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priv deploy - GitOps bridge proposal + diagram

Maria — thanks for the materials, this is very clear and a good starting point. Quick answers while we review the attachments: 

- CI gates: we typically require a successful "preflight" pipeline that runs terraform plan for network modules (read-only), helm lint + dry-run, and an integration smoke test that validates DNS/egress rules. We can provide the job names so your CI can gate on them.
- Secrets: Redwood prefers KMS-wrapped artifacts for operator-managed overlays, but we can support Vault agents for cluster-local secrets if you need dynamic credentials. We should pick one pattern per environment.
- Preflight matrix: I can draft a minimal matrix. Example checks: plan-no-changes for network modules, helm-template sanity, image provenance signature, kube-applier dry-run, basic namespace isolation tests.

Karthik / Kimberly — can you review the proposal and call out any hard blockers (especially around egress, IPAM and bastion jump configuration) before EOD PT?

Thanks,
Nikhil\Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acme.co>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 12:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priv deploy - GitOps bridge proposal + diagram

Adding a few concrete points from infra side: 

1) Terraform boundaries: keep network.tfstate read-only for the operator. We will map shared outputs to a read-only data source in the bridge namespace; no direct writes to tfstate from Redwood.

2) GitOps operator scope: operator will be restricted to the "rh-overlays" namespace and will only apply Helm/manifest overlays. We will require signed OCI images and SBOM checks in the pipeline.

3) CI integration: suggest these gates for your CI (names are what our GitOps expects):
   - tf-plan-network: runs terraform plan against the network modules, exits non-zero on drift.
   - helm-lint-and-dryrun: ensures templates render under target cluster values.
   - image-provenance-check: validates signature + provenance.
   - applier-dryrun: our operator simulates apply and reports forbidden changes (egress, hostNetwork, hostPath).

4) Network specifics: we need an explicit egress policy (CIDR allowlist) per namespace, and a documented bastion jump protocol (ssh certs via ACME or short-lived tokens). Also: IPAM allocation ranges must be provided ahead of pilot.

5) Ansible: For node bootstrap, we recommend Ansible roles live in your repo and our operator references the artifacts; we won't run Ansible against your control plane. That keeps separation of control.

I'll draft a minimal preflight matrix and a starter .gitlab-ci.yml snippet and drop links to them in the next message.

-Karthik
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Acme Infra Team <acme-infra@consultants.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acme.co>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priv deploy - GitOps bridge proposal + diagram

Thanks Karthik — that all looks doable. A few clarifications from our side: 

- IPAM: we'll carve out /20 per cluster and provide the tables by Monday.
- Secrets: we'll adopt KMS wrapping for operator artifacts for the initial pilot; Vault for per-pod secrets later in phase 2.
- CI job names: we can publish tf-plan-network and helm-lint-and-dryrun in our CI; image-provenance-check will require a small change to our build pipeline but it's on the roadmap.

We've also uploaded a short test harness for the applier-dryrun into the repo and left a README with how the operator will report blocked changes. Link: https://git.acme.co/ops/privbridge/test-harness

We'll aim to have the IPAM sheet and a first-pass CI snippet by Mon 2027-04-12.

—Acme Infra

- Redwood (Karthik): produce preflight matrix + .gitlab-ci.yml example for the applier-dryrun and image-provenance-check — ETA 2027-04-15
- Acme/Redwood: agree on secrets pattern for pilot (KMS wrap) and document key access flows — ETA 2027-04-16
- Kickoff pilot: target window 2027-04-26 to 2027-04-30 (tentative)

I'll open a tracking ticket in our shared workspace and attach the proposal and diagrams. If everyone agrees, please reply "ACK" to this thread and we'll lock dates.

Thanks all — excited to get the pilot running.

Regards,
Nikhil Sharma\Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
